# zstd / decompress_dstSize_tooSmall

zstd's own fuzz target `decompress_dstSize_tooSmall` ([source](source/decompress_dstSize_tooSmall.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over zstd (facebook/zstd at 82d322c4).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, an API contract: Compress the input at level 1, then decompress into a buffer strictly smaller than the input: must fail, and with exactly ZSTD_error_dstSize_tooSmall (empty input: must return 0).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against zstd at commit 82d322c4.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- ZSTD_compressCCtx into compressBound bytes must succeed ([lines 56-57](source/decompress_dstSize_tooSmall.c#L56-L57)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Compress the input at level 1, then decompress into a buffer strictly smaller than the input: must fail, and with exactly ZSTD_error_dstSize_tooSmall (empty input: must return 0) ([lines 56-64](source/decompress_dstSize_tooSmall.c#L56-L64)): abort(); confirmed in the binary.

A failure of the check at lines 56-64 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name it exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies it on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other check.
